evidence.claim: All likelihood numbers are FINDR editorial design heuristics, not manufacturer probabilities, prevalence, failure rates or calibrated diagnostic confidence. Unknown answers supply no evidence. Related observations are not guaranteed statistically independent.
evidence.limit: Ranking must remain a list of possibilities with an unresolved outcome; no percentage diagnosis or automatic repair recommendation.

evidence.claim: Supply monitoring can separately identify mains, disconnected battery, low battery, high impedance and charger conditions.

sourceRefs.section: §17 Power supply: displayed supply and battery faults

evidence.claim: Resistance in batteries or their leads can produce a supply fault; the indication alone does not identify the faulty part.

sourceRefs.section: §1.2 Power supply faults: high-resistance batteries or leads

evidence.claim: The cited Syncro powers the circuit from both OUT and IN when loop continuity is open. All expected addresses can therefore remain visible during an open-circuit fault.

sourceRefs.section: §9 Detection circuits: power from both OUT and IN after an open circuit

evidence.limit: This supports coexistence, not a promise that every break/short topology leaves every device available. A missing-device warning is not a continuity test.

evidence.claim: Short-circuit isolators can separate a faulty loop section while other loop portions remain available.

sourceRefs.section: §9 Detection circuits: power from both OUT and IN after an open circuit

evidence.claim: Bad data has several documented sources, including connections, interference, circuit leakage, excessive resistance and devices.

sourceRefs.section: §25.1 Loop Data Test: bad data and possible sources

evidence.limit: No observation here identifies a particular component or proves that interference is present.

evidence.claim: Advanced describes extra resistance/partial-short monitoring, but its enabled state depends on firmware/configuration.

sourceRefs.section: Hardware Features / Wiring fault monitoring (PDF page 7, left-hand printed page 12)
v60.03.00: EN54-13 monitoring disabled as default

evidence.claim: Hochiki lists an earth fault, including water ingress, among loop-communication causes; Syncro defines an earth-fault detection condition.

Questions about prior work, weather and configuration changes collect chronology. Their links to candidate causes are editorial hypotheses, not manufacturer statements that correlation proves a cause.
The GENT message list defines a lost device as one that is not communicating; it does not by itself establish detector failure.
The Syncro manual describes duplicate addresses; Hochiki includes physical-device/list mismatch among communication-fault causes.
